narrative: Pearl remains a 1-month-old-in-spirit but fast-moving project four months post-mainnet: price has firmed to ~$0.29 (its best level in over three weeks) on modest volume, while chain activity continues uninterrupted with block height past 105,500. Bridge custody, minted WPRL, and surplus all reconcile cleanly with no anomalies. GitHub cadence picked back up on the core node repo (3 commits in the last 7 days after a quieter stretch), and the ecosystem catalog grew with the addition of an independent explorer (pearlchain.live), a PRC-20 inscription marketplace, and another mining pool — evidence the community keeps shipping tooling around the chain faster than a one-month-old project typically would.

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height is well past the fork — the fix remains live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields remain null pending a replacement public data source.

The bridge relay's /api/custody endpoint briefly reported a negative surplus (WPRL supply ~28,800 PRL above locked PRL), driven by its lockGrains field reading well below an independent read of the same address. WPRL total supply was independently confirmed correct via a direct Ethereum RPC call to the contract's totalSupply(). prlscan's own ledger for the lock address (received minus sent, self-consistent) put its balance about 38,900 PRL higher than the relay reported, and no single recent transaction in that address's history explains a real shortfall of that size — pointing to a bug or stale field in the relay's custody rollup rather than an actual funding gap. TVL and surplus fields were null in that snapshot pending relay-side confirmation.

The relay custody-data issue from 2026-08-03 worsened before it was fixed: /api/custody's lockGrains briefly read a flat 0 for the lock address, with the reported deficit widening to roughly -76,300 PRL. Re-verified independently via prlscan's own ledger (address holds a real, non-zero balance) and a fresh Ethereum RPC call confirming /api/supply matched the true on-chain WPRL total exactly.

Resolved: the relay custody-data issue tracked on 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-04 was fixed. /api/custody's lockGrains and totalSupplyGrains matched independent verification exactly — prlscan's lock-address ledger and a direct Ethereum RPC totalSupply() call both agreed with the relay byte-for-byte. At no point during the episode did it appear in public social discussion, consistent with it having been an internal relay-monitoring bug rather than anything user-facing.
